title: A Road With No Waymarks
reflection:
The Camino's yellow arrows guided you for years, each one confirming you were still on the right path, still counting the distance to somewhere. Today's road has no arrows — just open country and your own two feet.

This isn't the end of the pilgrimage. It's a new stretch of the same road, walked without a waymark to check yourself against.
closing: God of the unmarked road, walk this open stretch with me. I don't need an arrow to know you are near. Amen.

scripture.text: I am about to do a new thing; now it springs forth, do you not perceive it?

title: What the Miles Taught
reflection:
Every stretch you ever walked, every blister you tended and kept going through, trained a pilgrim who is still walking. None of those miles were wasted, even the hardest ones.

Let yourself remember them today with gratitude rather than grief. The road behind you shaped the one ahead.
closing: Thank you for the miles behind me. Let their wisdom walk with me still. Amen.

scripture.text: Hitherto the Lord has helped us.

title: Walking Without the Weather Report
reflection:
No monthly storm to check the forecast for now — just an ordinary day's walking, its conditions steadier than they've been in a long while.

There can be a grief in that steadiness, and a relief in it too, sometimes both in the same mile. Let today hold whichever one shows up.
closing: God of steady weather, thank you for this calm stretch. Where there's grief inside it, receive that too. Amen.

scripture.text: Be still, and know that I am God.

title: Country Wide Enough for This
reflection:
No distance to track, no waymark to follow, no pack to weigh against tomorrow's stage — just the walk itself, wide open in front of you.

That width can feel disorienting before it feels spacious. Let it become room instead: space to walk exactly as today asks, unscheduled by anything but grace.
closing: God of open country, thank you for this widened road. Teach me to walk it freely. Amen.

scripture.text: You will show me the path of life; in your presence there is fullness of joy.

title: A Fellow Pilgrim Still
reflection:
Roads change. Stages change. What has walked beside you through every one of them has not.

However unfamiliar this stretch of country feels, you are not walking it for the first time alone. The same companion who kept pace on the Camino keeps pace in the wide country too.
closing: Thank you for staying, mile after changing mile. Walk on with me now. Amen.

scripture.text: I am with you always, to the very end of the age.
